These are prior-based estimates; I didn't run anything against NAS-Bench-201 data. They rest on general patterns in this search space:

- **Convolutions matter most.** They drive accuracy.
- **Skip on edge 3 helps.** It acts as a residual connection.
- **Substitution effect.** Adding a conv helps more when the other paths are weak (none or pooling) than when they already carry convs.
- **Same-edge conditions depend on what is replaced.** When the condition is on the edited edge, the effect is relative to the op being replaced. Replacing a weak op tends to gain more than the average replacement.

Most interactions are probably small or inconsistent across datasets, so most numbers sit near 40–55.
